scope: Bounded redistribution of already assigned audited SMP-ready tasks to empty CPU queues.

implementation.owner: Private sched/task/balance.rs uses the existing task registry and runtime admission; no new public API, module, scheduler instance or registry.
implementation.trigger: Empty local queues try at dispatch, idle recheck, idle timer and reschedule entry. Ready publication tries one empty idle destination and sends its reschedule IPI after transfer. A source keeps at least one Ready task. Donor selection uses at most32 CPU slots; one donor, at most8 rotating task candidates per attempt.
implementation.admission: Explicitly SMP eligible, Ready/linked, no physical running/current source task, CPU affinity, driver/async execution owner, held locks/preemption/permit handoff, outstanding wait or teardown. FPU backing must be valid when used. Merely observing Ready never proves the physical stack is free.
implementation.preserved: Unlink/append to an empty destination retains ready order/time, role/priority/donation budgets, generation, saved RSP/FPU and exact task unwind counter. No activation reset, allocation or wait. Transfer/home/pending/IPI publish under one runtime admission. Explicit forced CPU bindings remain fixed, including offline refusal. Existing physical-switch/IRQ/FPU release bodies unchanged.
implementation.anti_pingpong: Only empty target versus at least2 Ready source tasks; per-task minimum one quantum since the last migration. Rotating donor and candidate cursors avoid a permanent bound prefix.
implementation.limits: Only previously audited SMP classes; driver/async owners remain on their assigned CPU even if explicitly parallel. No public affinity contract, hotplug migration, NUMA/topology policy, fairness latency guarantee or already measured speedup.

source_audit.preserved: All original physical switch/RSP release, IRQ/EOI/FPU handling, exact task unwind binding, sleep/wake and task resource teardown bodies unchanged. Shared append only adds cursor storage; balancing alone retains old ready order. Public ABI/TaskView/Contract/SDK/Spectra unchanged. Fixed affinities now have a distinct internal marker; direct driver/async owners remain excluded.
source_audit.scope: Source preservation audit, not an extra runtime test or concurrency/speedup proof.

scoped_guest.scope: Original owned SMP/TLB and native scheduler/role/IF/FPU/deadline checks, with one required uneven-ready-queue extension. Four already-started own tasks, real YMM and exact unwind tokens, pinned rejection, preserved ready facts and real final retirement. No public API or permanent observer.
scoped_guest.limits: Actual normal SMP4 acceptance; original functional oracles preserved. One added native case for the new migration boundary. No exhaustive interleaving, locality speedup or fairness latency bound claim.
scoped_guest.rebalance_marker: TASKREG08427 rebalance PASS tasks=4 migrated=2 pinned=1 fpu=4 unwind=4 ready=preserved own=retired

comparison_previous.observation: One final run per artifact; descriptive comparison without causal gain/parity claim. All deltas retained, unchanged workload/reference, no score-selection rerun.

test_policy: One normal SMP4 guest bundles existing native scheduler sync/unwind/roles/deadlines/FPU and exact SMP/TLB/owner cases. Add only the missing four-task wake/migration boundary within live fairness: real sleeping stacks, YMM, exact unwind tokens, pinned Ready refusal, ready/budget preservation and final task retirement. No new suite, microbenchmark or broad catalogue. Below three schedulable CPUs the extension explicitly reports unavailable and leaves original fairness cases intact.

performance_policy.reason: Scheduler/Ready and wake publication paths affect runtime; exactly one final STANDARD Suite2 SMP4 with unchanged full DevCenter import/GET5/30/6valid. Descriptive comparison to 0.84.26 adb7726f-7ba2-4d75-91d5-705da49b4851; unchanged method/reference.
